exposure: changes in sonographic cervical length (CL) measured at 14-16 and 21-24 weeks of gestation
Change in sonographic cervical length (CL) between 14-16 weeks and 21-24 weeks gestation
cervical shortening < 10% between CL(1) and CL(2)
finding: A decrease in cervical length of 10% or more between 14-16 weeks and 21-24 weeks gestation was associated with lower use of cervical ripening at term.
mod_finding: This study did not examine mode of delivery as a primary or secondary outcome.
